quotes.text: We get jumped by the Socs. I'm not sure how you spell it, but it's the abbreviation for the Socials, the jet set, the West-side rich kids.
quotes.reference: 1967, S. E. Hinton, The Outsiders, page 2:

senses.definition: (UK, university slang) A society (circle, club, interest group).
examples: Are you part of any socs this year?

senses.definition: (UK, law, historical) The lord's power or privilege of holding a court in a district, as in manor or lordship; jurisdiction of causes, and the limits of that jurisdiction.

quotes.text: As proprietors of the soc, the lords claimed a great number of fees and perquisites, payable by all classes of people, whether free or servile, who negotiated any affairs within the soc, and which no doubt formed in themselves a considerable source of revenue.
quotes.reference: 1869, George Norton, Commentaries on the History, Constitution, and Chartered Franchises of the City of London, page 96:

quotes.text: Doubts have recently been cast upon Maitland's view that the Anglo-Saxon "sac and soc" included the right to hold a petty court, to compel tenants to attend it, and to take profits from it.
quotes.reference: 2001, Theodore Frank Thomas Plucknett, A Concise History of the Common Law, page 96:

senses.definition: (UK, obsolete) An exclusive privilege formerly claimed by millers of grinding all the corn used within the manor or township in which the mill stands.
